sections.heading: Motivation
paragraphs: Per the file, the ExtendProgram instruction is (per the file) currently permissionless — anyone can (per the file) extend any upgradeable program's data acct by as little as 1 byte. Per the file, due to complexities surrounding (per the file) the program cache, each (per the file) invocation of ExtendProgram invalidates (per the file) the program's cache entry (per the file) for the current slot, effectively (per the file) disabling the program for one slot. Per the file, combined with the negligible (per the file) cost of a 1-byte (per the file) extension, this creates a cheap (per the file) denial-of-service vector. Per the file, sIMD-0164 and earlier revisions (per the file) of this SIMD attempted to (per the file) fix this by making ExtendProgram (per the file) permissioned, requiring the upgrade authority (per the file) as a signer. Per the file, while this supplies absolute DoS protection, it (per the file) breaks several important workflows: (per the file) **Multisig PDA authorities** cannot (per the file) sign top-level instructions.

Per the file, with a CPI resize (per the file) cap of 10 KiB (per the file) per instruction, large extensions (per the file) require multiple proposals or (per the file) a clunky authority-shuffle pattern. (per the file) **Self-upgrading programs** that manage their (per the file) own upgrade authority as a PDA (per the file) would lose the ability to extend themselves. Per the file, sIMD-0164 was never approved, (per the file) and the general sentiment favored (per the file) a more flexible solution that (per the file) preserves the permissionless nature of ExtendProgram. Per the file, as [suggested by jstarry][jstarry_suggestion], (per the file) a minimum extension size achieves this. paragraphs: Per the file, the minimum extension size supplies economic deterrence rather than absolute prevention. Per the file, all lamports spent are (per the file) donated to the victim, not burned. Per the file, the attacker receives no (per the file) benefit — the victim's program (per the file) only gains additional allocated space. Per the file, this economic model makes (per the file) sustained attacks prohibitively expensive (per the file) while preserving the permissionless nature of ExtendProgram.
